# SNDK — Catalysts

## TL;DR

Q3 FY2026 earnings printed 2026-04-30 — blowout beat that drove the parabolic move to $1,256 intraday. Next scheduled binary is Q4 FY2026 earnings (~August 13, 2026; consensus EPS $29.93). No catalyst within the 10-trading-day swing window as of 2026-05-04. Sell-side has upgraded sharply post-print: 29 Buy / 4 Hold / 0 Sell, avg PT $1,341 (range $650–$2,000). [source: web_research/SNDK.json, run 20260504_212836]

## Upcoming events

- **Q4 FY2026 earnings:** Expected ~August 13, 2026 (consensus EPS $29.93). ~55+ trading days out — well outside swing window. [source: web_research/SNDK.json earnings_info, run 20260504_212836]
- **$6B share buyback execution:** Authorized 2026-04-30; pace will be disclosed quarterly. Active through FY2027. [source: web_research/SNDK.json ticker_news, run 20260504_212836]
- **QLC Stargate datacenter SSD ramp:** Management referenced readiness for ramp in coming quarters during the Q3 FY2026 call. No specific date confirmed. [source: signals_combined.json swing_catalyst_news SNDK, run 20260504_212836]
- **Any incremental hyperscaler contract announcements:** No scheduled date — track as ad-hoc disclosures.
- **Sell-side conference circuit (May–June 2026):** Pending; typical venues include BofA Tech and Bernstein Strategic Decisions.

## Recent news synthesis (last 14 days)

- **2026-05-04 — 24/7 Wall St bearish caution:** "SanDisk Stock's 3,314% Rally Leaves Little Room to Run" — valuation risk noted; ~32% downside scenario. [source: web_research/SNDK.json ticker_news]
- **2026-05-03 — $42B supply agreements confirmed:** SanDisk disclosed $42B in long-term hyperscaler supply agreements alongside Q3 results. [source: web_research/SNDK.json ticker_news]
- **2026-05-01 — SNDK +17.6% for the week / best S&P 500 stock 2026:** +361% YTD as of May 4, after earnings gap +8%+ on May 1. [source: web_research/SNDK.json ticker_news]
- **2026-04-30 — Q3 FY2026 earnings:** Revenue $5.95B (+251% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $23.41 (beat $14.66 consensus by 61.4%), gross margin 78.4%, datacenter revenue $1.47B (+645% YoY), five multi-year hyperscaler contracts, $42B minimum revenue backlog. [source: web_research/SNDK.json earnings_info]

## Insider activity

Aggregate ~$7.3M across 20 Form 4 filings — primarily RSU tax withholdings (CEO David Goeckeler 1,569 shares at $632.38; CTO Alper Ilkbahar 566 shares at $632.38) plus one estate-planning gift (director Thomas Caulfield gifted 29,000 shares). No open-market conviction purchases. Sentiment: mildly negative lean but low-signal (typical RSU mechanics, not directional bets). [source: signals_combined.json swing_catalyst_news SNDK, run 20260504_212836]

## Analyst consensus

Rating: **Buy** (29 Buy / 4 Hold / 0 Sell). Avg PT $1,341 (range $650–$2,000). Post-earnings upgrades: Susquehanna $1,000→$2,000; Cantor Fitzgerald →$1,800; Bernstein →$1,700; Evercore ISI $1,200→$1,400; Raymond James $725→$1,470; Goldman Sachs $700→$1,200; Morgan Stanley $690→$1,100. No recent downgrades. Current price ~$1,256 intraday / $1,187 daily close is within or above the buy consensus range — the upgrade cycle may be largely priced. [source: web_research/SNDK.json analyst_consensus, run 20260504_212836]

## Competitor context

Samsung and SK Hynix exercising disciplined NAND capex, supporting pricing. SK Hynix pivoting to HBM, ceding enterprise SSD share to SNDK. Micron also emphasizing HBM over commodity NAND. SNDK's pure-play NAND positioning (spun off WD in 2025) is a differentiator. [source: web_research/SNDK.json competitor_activity, run 20260504_212836]

## Lessons

2026-04-30 | NVDA | EMA pullback Fib dip-buy | -$63.20 (corrected from -$264.65) | Stop triggered at $205.30 (hourly Fib 61.8%); swing_trend_momentum and swing_breakout were bullish on AI capex thesis, but price breached the stop zone intraday amid stretched macro (RSI 81–87) with no bullish confirmation candle before exit. **Note:** trade was originally sized 67 shares ($14,020) due to a phantom $100K budget bug (fixed commit b2b472d). With the correct $25K budget at 14.2% vol-adj limit, position would have been 16 shares ($3,348). Corrected P&L reflects the strategy's actual signal quality, not the sizing error.
